summary: Uzbekistan’s restoration commitments include forest-cover targets of 4.5 million and 6.1 million hectares, with 2.3 million hectares for Aral Sea afforestation; planting one billion trees and shrubs over five years; growing 919 million trees by 2030; and raising forest cover to 15%, versus 0.1% currently mapped. Other goals include 30% greening by 2026 and 100,000 hectares of water management in Southern Karakalpakstan. The Aral Sea afforestation pledge equals about 34.6 times current mapped forest area. Conservation aims to expand protected natural territories to 14.5% in 2025 and 17% by 2030, with a 12% strategy goal, while a conservation target sets forest cover at 4.1 million hectares. Agriculture includes up to 1 million hectares of drip irrigation, 2 million hectares of water-saving technology, yield increases of 20–40% and 30–35%, and 25% better water-use efficiency; a 1-million-hectare irrigation area equals about 11.3% of current mapped agricultural land.
